items.title: Archimedean super-rigidity in the author's centreless real-algebraic setting
items.difficulty_reason: After old Margulis/Howe-Moore/Furstenberg inputs, H-orbit rationality, finite conjugate generation, one-orbit reduction and all actually selected old nonarch arguments are given, the new archimedean proof still has to convert almost-everywhere equivariance into global analytic boundary regularity. It descends a rational map through real-point finite-cover/product geometry to a Zariski open analytic map, propagates that map across conjugate H-actions to all G/P0, then removes word-choice ambiguity using a Zariski-normalised stabilizer and recovers an analytic ambient homomorphism from a finite tuple with trivial stabilizer. This source-local regularity and reconstruction chain is substantial research-level rigidity; neither the old theorem nor a direct standard-theorem substitution supplies it.
